about: The round 1 progress page's own words and the files each section reads. work/build/scripts/phase-3/progress_round_1_build.py reads this file on every run; every number and picture on the page comes from the files named under slots, read at build time. A {name} in a sentence is filled from those files. Codes in a 'refs' field print only in the small reference lines.
title: Edition 06 Round 1 Progress

cover.title: Round 1, as it stands
cover.deck_rescored: Round 1 drew chapter 14’s first four families of charts, wrote its rules for every chart and built the first part of chapter 15. This page shows that work after the review, the fix pass and the creative director’s second scores.
cover.deck_building: Round 1 drew chapter 14’s first four families of charts, wrote its rules for every chart and built the first part of chapter 15. This page shows that work as built, while its review runs. It fills in again once the fix pass and the creative director’s second scores land.
cover.no_decision: This page asks you nothing. Board 2 follows round 3, and that is where you decide.
cover.minutes: Pictures show at true size. Where one is wider than your window, its frame scrolls sideways.

round.title: Round 1 in one screen
round.dol_frozen: Frozen as {dol_file}, {dol_rows} rows, research ledger row {dol_row}.
round.dol_waiting: Saved as you sent it. The research lead’s notes do not yet record it frozen for round 3’s row 113.

charts.title: The {n_new} new charts
charts.lede: Each chart as the chart kit draws it, from the kit’s own pictures. The first pair is on Newsprint and the second on Charcoal; in each, the drawing for a 1440 px page sits beside the drawing for a 390 px phone page. The line under each pair gives the chart’s size in the guide and the result of the kit’s own check.

entry.title: How an entry reads in the guide
entry.lede: Every form in chapter 14 gets one numbered entry in the same order: the rule, when to use the form, what to use instead, why it works, then its example chart with the chart’s table. Here is Rule {entry_rule}, “{entry_title}”, photographed from today’s guide at a 1440 px window and at a 390 px window.

sketches.title: The {n_sketch_w} sketches
sketches.lede: {n_sketch_cap} forms get a small sketch with invented, labeled data in place of a finished chart: {n_avoid_w} the guide tells builders to avoid, and {n_ref_w} it keeps for reference. Each is shown with the heading the guide prints over it, photographed at a 1440 px window.

rules.title: Rules {r_first} to {r_last}, for every chart
rules.lede: Chapter 14 opens with {n_ch_rules} rules that hold for every chart. Each rule has two plates, the framed examples under it: a correct one and a failure. Both are photographed from today’s guide at a 1440 px window, side by side where they fit and one above the other where they do not. The chapter’s opening plate comes first.

ch15.title: Chapter 15’s round 1 plates
ch15.lede: Round 1 built chapter 15’s opener and {n15} of its rules, {n15_plates} plates in all. Each plate is photographed from today’s guide at a 1440 px window and at a 390 px window, side by side. Every plate is drawn at one true size at every width, so the two pictures differ only where the words wrap.

scores.title: Scores
scores.cd_lede: The creative director scores {cd_items_w} parts of round 1 from 1 to 5 on {cd_crit_w} counts: {cd_crit}. A part ships at 4 or more on every count.
scores.cd_lede_wait: The creative director scores each part of round 1 from 1 to 5 on each count of the studio’s rubric. A part ships at 4 or more on every count.
scores.legend_first: Each cell shows the first score. A cell with a frame is under 4.
scores.legend_both: Each cell shows the first score in small type, then the second score after the fix pass. A shaded cell moved. A cell with a frame is under 4.
scores.cd_wait: The creative director’s first scores join this table when their file lands.
scores.cd_re_wait: The second scores, after the fix pass, join this table when their file lands; each cell then shows both.
scores.rt_lede: {n_rt_cap} reviewers read round 1 beside the creative director, each from one side. Each gives a score from 1 to 5 and numbers what it found.
scores.rt_note: Must fix means a fault that breaks a rule, misleads or blocks a task. Should fix means a fault that weakens the work. Each count is read from the report’s own numbered findings.

weight.title: Weight
weight.lede: The guide is one file, so every chart adds to what a reader downloads. These figures come from the build report of today’s strict build.
weight.fig_caption: Each bar shows how much of its limit a part uses today.

rows.page: The whole guide, projected, against {budget_mb} MB

weight.per_plate: Chapter 14 weighs {ch14_bytes} bytes against its stop of {ch14_stop} bytes. That leaves {per_plate} bytes for each of the {plates_to_come} finished charts still to come, after the room the kit and the chapter’s other parts still need.
weight.ch15_line: Chapter 15 weighs {ch15_bytes} bytes against its ceiling of {ch15_ceiling}.
weight.page_line: The guide weighs {page_bytes} bytes today. With every chapter still to come counted at its full allocation, it projects to {proj_bytes} bytes, {proj_room} bytes under the {budget_mb} MB the page may reach.

tested.title: Tested and not tested
tested.lede: What each owner and reviewer checked, kept apart from what they did not, as their files list it. Each column opens on what was not tested.
tested.path_note: Quoted from the teammates’ files. Paths into the studio’s private working folder read [scratch], and decision codes move to the reference line.

next.title: Next
next.line: Round 2 builds composition, distribution and density, correlation, uncertainty and estimates, and gauges and indicators.
